instrument: xml insert hook — the 1.83x `contains` factor, explained to the edge
status: RESOLVED. It is not an instrument artifact and not this lane's defect: it is a duplicated-edge defect in the SHARED indexer, and it fires for every owned symbol whose name contains a colon.
theQuestion: 300 libxslt files: `contains` emitted 4,375 through parseFile, stored 7,649 = 1.748x, while calls/imports were exactly 1.0 and references 0.91. One-file probe: tests/docbook/common/common.xsl emitted 294 contains edges, the store held 511.

mechanism.where: src/ast/parallel-indexer.ts — the auto-generated containment pass (#756 / M51.A1): for every symbol with an owner, if the engine has not already emitted that containment it BUFFERS one `contains` row (`:3955-3984`, `:4208-4213`).
mechanism.theDefect: THE DEDUP KEY IS BUILT WITH ONE SHAPE AND LOOKED UP WITH ANOTHER. The key set is built from the analyzer's contains edges with BOTH ENDS LEAF-REDUCED — `containsPairs.add(`${srcLeaf} ${tgtLeaf}`)` via `/^.*:([^:]+):?\d*$/` (`:3651-3659`). The lookup reduces only the OWNER and leaves the CHILD RAW — `containsPairs.has(`${ownerLeaf} ${symbol.name}`)` (`:3971-3972`). For any name containing a colon the two keys differ by construction, the guard never fires, and a containment edge the analyzer already emitted is written a SECOND time.
mechanism.whyXml: prefixed names are the norm in this lane (`xsl:template`, `doc:reference`, `xsl:value-of`), so 217 of the file's 292 owned symbols take the second path.
mechanism.notAHypothesis: predicted with the indexer's own two regexes from the symbol table: 217 owned symbols whose lookup key is absent from the leaf-reduced key set — all 217 colon-named — against a measured difference of exactly 217. MATCH: true (validation/m14/fixtures/xml/insert-hook.json counts.synthesizedPredicted vs counts.storedContainsMinusAnalyzer).

whatItMeans.forThisLane: The lane's four-clause numbers do NOT move: the residual gate is a key-space model over analyzer output and never reads the store; every store-derived figure is a ratio over the stored set, and a duplicated row is one more row of the same (owner, child) pair, so it does not change a binding verdict. The 120-file draw's percentages are affected only in their DENOMINATOR and are already labelled as one run.
whatItMeans.fleet: Every lane whose symbols carry a colon in their name gets duplicate containment edges. xml is measured; the condition is mechanical (a colon in the child symbol's name) so other lanes can be checked by counting colon-named owned symbols in their stores.
whatItMeans.fixBelongsToTheSharedIndexer: make the two key shapes agree — leaf-reduce the child in the lookup, or key the pair set on resolved ids like the row identity already does. `src/ast/parallel-indexer.ts` is not this lane's file, so this is REPORTED, not edited.

howItWasFound: The Lead's order was one file with an insert hook. The hook recorded ZERO inserts because the store runs in worker threads, where a main-thread driver patch is invisible — which itself is a fact worth keeping: any probe that patches better-sqlite3 in the main thread sees nothing. The answer came from the store side instead: analyzer edges beside stored rows for one file, then the indexer's own regexes replayed in the probe to predict the exact difference.

whySymmetricIsWorse.answer: THE OWNER REGEX, and it is a one-line A/B as the Lead suspected. The build-site regex `/^.*:([^:]+):?\d*$/` applied to an `ownerSymbolId` — which ends `:<line>` — captures the LINE NUMBER as the leaf: `proj:…:xsl:stylesheet:1` -> `1`, not `stylesheet`, because `.*:` is greedy to the last colon and `\d*$` then matches the empty string. The ORIGINAL lookup regex `/^.*:([^:]+):\d+$/` anchors the digit-run into the required `:\d+$` suffix, so the NAME is captured instead. Making the owner regex 'consistent' therefore breaks the ownerLeaf for every symbol id (all of them end in a line number) and 48,085 MORE rows are synthesized.
whySymmetricIsWorse.consequenceForTheGuard: `containsPairs` IS NOT a leaf-keyed set in the way its build site suggests. The same regex that produces a usable leaf from a NAME produces a LINE NUMBER from an ID, so no repair may reuse it on both sides. A shape-appropriate leaf function is required — strip a trailing `:<digits>` from ids first, then take the last colon segment — or, better, key the pair set on resolved symbol ids the way the row identity already does.

theFix.methodNoteKept: The main-thread insert hook recorded 0 inserts: the store writes in worker threads, where a main-thread `better-sqlite3` patch is invisible. The experiment was run through the store-side probe instead, which is the instrument that can see the rows.
